'''''Dichondra argentea''''', the '''silver ponysfoot''' or '''silver nickel vine''', is a species of flowering plant in the family [[Convolvulaceae]].<ref name="MBG_259475" >{{cite web |url=https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=259475 |title=''Dichondra argentea'' 'Silver Falls' |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=2022 |website=Plant Finder |publisher=Missouri Botanical Garden |access-date=10 September 2022 }}</ref> 

==Description==
It is a [[xerophytic]], [[groundcover|creeping]], climbing, fast-growing plant reaching {{cvt|4|in|cm|0}} high but growing {{cvt|4|to|6|ft|m|0}} long. Its stems are short, very branched. The dark green leaves are simple, entire, alternate, kidney-shaped or ear-shaped. They are 1–2 × 2 cm; cleft apex. 

The whitish flowers are isolated, on recurved [[Pedicel (botany)|pedicel]]s. They are barely visible and have a diameter of 5 mm. The fruit is a [[globose]], cleft capsule, 5 mm in diameter, hairy. Dark brown to black seeds, 2 mm long, with short, white hairs.<ref name="MBG_259475" />

==Cultivation==
It is hardy in [[Hardiness zone|USDA zones]] 10 through 12. In cultivation it is grown as annual, chiefly as a hanging accent plant or ground cover. There is a cultivar, 'Silver Falls'.<ref name="RHS_219360" >{{cite web |title=''Dichondra argentea'' 'Silver Falls' silver nickel vine 'Silver Falls' |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/219360/i-dichondra-argentea-i-silver-falls/details |date=2022 |publisher=The Royal Horticultural Society |access-date=10 September 2022 |quote=Synonyms; ''Dichondra micrantha'' 'Silver Falls' }}</ref>

==Distribution==
It is disjunctly distributed in New Mexico, Texas, Mexico, Colombia, Bolivia, northwest Argentina, and southeast Brazil, and has gone extinct in Arizona.<ref name="POWO_267747-1" >{{cite POWO |id=267747-1 |title=''Dichondra argentea'' Willd. |access-date=10 September 2022 }}</ref>

==Uses==
This plant is popularly known as a remedy for [[bile]] in the north of the Mexican Republic, in the states of [[Aguascalientes]] and [[Durango]]. It is also ingested as an [[Appetite stimulant|appetizer]], [[laxative]] and anti-abortive, in this case, due to its property of relaxing the [[uterine]] muscle. It is also used to avoid having children. It is also used against [[heart problem]]s, ant bites, bitterness in the mouth, headaches, to regulate fever and relieve toothache, [[tonsillitis]] and pain due to anger. 

At the beginning of the 18th century, [[Juan de Esteyneffer]] used it in a [[decoction]] against protruding [[tripe]]. In the 20th century, Maximino Martínez mentions it as an [[anti-inflammatory]]; against bilious diseases, and points out that it causes [[idiocy]].
